title: MRP vs Recent Selling Price in India: What to Trust During a Sale
description: MRP is a legal ceiling inclusive of all taxes, not a record of what a product usually sells for. During a sale, compare the final payable against a dated recent price for the same exact model code — never against the strike-through alone.

forWho: Shoppers comparing a sale price against a 'was' price or MRP on an Indian store page.
Anyone who wants a dated same-SKU baseline before deciding whether a discount is real.
skipIf: Anyone looking for a universal 'true price' formula — a baseline exists only when an identical model code has a dated price on another page.
Readers who want first-hand testing. This page uses official rules and dated listings checked 25 Nov 2026; Durza did not buy or test any product.

content_blocks.body: Use MRP only as a legal ceiling: rule 2(m) of the Packaged Commodities Rules defines it as the maximum price inclusive of all taxes, and rule 18(2) prohibits selling above it. It is not a usual-price benchmark. For a real saving, compare the final payable against a dated price for the identical model code from another page. On 25 Nov 2026 the same ASUS FA401EA-RG020WS carried a ₹3,23,990 MRP at ASUS eStore but a ₹2,59,990 reference at Flipkart — sources disagree, so verify on the exact SKU at checkout. A headline percentage off MRP is not, by itself, evidence of a real saving: confirm the exact SKU and the basis of the comparison before treating any saving as realised.

content_blocks.heading: What we verified, and what we did not
items: We verified the MRP definition, tax-inclusive rule, no-sale-above-MRP rule and e-commerce display duty from official documents opened 25 Nov 2026, along with dated CCPA drip-pricing penalties in a Rajya Sabha reply from 4 Aug 2026. Durza did not buy, consume or wear any product.
We did not verify how common padded MRPs are during Black Friday — no prevalence source was opened. Do not read this page as a claim that most sale banners are inflated.

Tracker figures are third-party records, not live quotes. Where a tracker and a store listing disagree by a few hundred rupees on the same model code, we show both and tell you to verify on the store rather than averaging them.
Confidence levels: label each figure as officially published, third-party recorded, manufacturer claim or unverified, and do not generalise a single tracked observation into a market-wide conclusion.

content_blocks.heading: MRP is a ceiling, not a baseline
paragraphs: Rule 2(m) of the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 defines retail sale price as the maximum price at which a packaged commodity may be sold, inclusive of all taxes (official text checked 25 Nov 2026). Rule 18(2) says no seller may charge above it. That makes MRP a legal ceiling — it does not tell you what a product usually sold for last month.

The Department of Consumer Affairs FAQ says a lower revised MRP may be shown only while the original remains visible and legible (rule 6(3) proviso, checked 25 Nov 2026). A big gap between MRP and the selling price is therefore not, on its own, proof of a good deal.

content_blocks.heading: How to build a same-SKU baseline
paragraphs: Match the full model code, not the series name. For example, Lenovo LOQ 15IRX9 is a series containing distinct MTMs such as 83DV01KYIN and 83DV01K7IN with different processors, storage and availability. A tracker record for 83DV01AAIN showed ₹1,04,990 on 1 Nov 2026 and ₹1,17,990 on 24 Nov 2026 — by our arithmetic, the later price was 12.38% higher. These are third-party records; verify on the store.

Another tracker record shows 83DV00BHIN at ₹87,999 on 20 Mar 2026 versus ₹1,14,690 on 23 Nov 2026, with a 933-day average of ₹85,924. Using a December 2024 low as a 2026 baseline would be misleading — keep the baseline inside the same year and the same exact code.

content_blocks.heading: A revealed sale price is not a payable price
paragraphs: Nykaa's price-reveal page checked 25 Nov 2026 showed L'Oréal Extraordinary Oil Serum at a regular ₹799, a current ₹719 and a revealed Pink Friday price of ₹439. Against the current price that is 38.94% additional saving by our arithmetic on published figures; against the list price it is 45.06%. The reveal is not yet a payable price — verify when the sale goes live.

For packaged goods, the official GST FAQ says GST is included in MRP and cannot be charged over it. Checkout additions were the subject of CCPA penalties recorded in the 4 Aug 2026 Rajya Sabha reply: FirstCry was penalised ₹2,00,000 for charging GST over an 'inclusive of all taxes' MRP, and Zepto ₹7,00,000 for adding handling and membership fees at checkout.

items.q: Is MRP the usual selling price in India?
items.a: No. MRP is the maximum tax-inclusive price defined in rule 2(m) of the Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011; rule 18(2) prohibits selling above it (official text checked 25 Nov 2026). It is a ceiling, not a recent-price benchmark.

items.q: Can a store charge GST over MRP?
items.a: The official Legal Metrology GST FAQ states GST is included in MRP and is not to be charged over MRP (checked 25 Nov 2026).

items.q: What counts as a fair baseline?
items.a: The identical full model code or exact item on a dated page from a regular sale — never MRP and never a different variant. Tracker records are third-party; verify on the store.

items.q: Does a 75% strike-through mean 75% off the real price?
items.a: It means 75% off MRP by our arithmetic on published figures. For GoBoult Anchor, ₹2,499 against ₹9,999 MRP is 75.01% off MRP; the saving against its recent selling price is a different number and is not sourced here.

items.q: Has anyone been penalised for checkout price tricks?
items.a: The Rajya Sabha reply dated 4 Aug 2026 records CCPA penalties of ₹2,00,000 on FirstCry and ₹7,00,000 on Zepto for drip pricing, among actions totalling ₹20 lakh.
